name: chirality
doc:
CHIRALITY & ASYMMETRIC AUTOCATALYSIS - the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry (Kagan & Soai, "non-linear
effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis"). SEALED through chemistry.CHEM_VERIFY: the
enantiomeric-excess arithmetic and the amplification SIGNATURE (product ee exceeds seed ee). The lab
discovery - that this happens, and runs toward homochirality - is Kagan's and Soai's, CITED, never
sealed by the engine. The one-handedness of life (L-amino acids, D-sugars) is carried as the open
question it answers. Idempotent. Matt, 2026-10-13: "Look at what they found." New stick.

sticks.question: Chirality and asymmetric autocatalysis
sticks.statement: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry (Kagan & Soai). Enantiomeric excess measures one-handedness; a small excess can be amplified - the product's ee exceeds the catalyst's (Kagan's non-linear effect), and in Soai's asymmetric autocatalysis the product is its own catalyst, so the excess runs toward homochirality (one source, a small bias, one end).
references: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026 (H. B. Kagan, K. Soai), nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2026
H. B. Kagan et al., nonlinear effects in asymmetric synthesis, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 108 (1986) 2353
K. Soai et al., asymmetric autocatalysis, Nature 378 (1995) 767

marks.claim: [one-handedness, measured] A 99:1 mixture of the two mirror images has enantiomeric excess ee = |R-S|/(R+S) x 100% = |99-1|/100 = 98% (sealed through chemistry.CHEM_VERIFY) - how far a sample leans to a single hand.
[the symmetric start] A 50:50 mixture is racemic: ee = 0% (sealed) - no handedness, the field a tiny bias breaks.

[amplification - the Kagan-Soai signature] When product ee (95%) EXCEEDS seed ee (5%), a small handedness has been amplified: a positive non-linear effect (sealed). Soai's asymmetric autocatalysis - the product catalyzing its own formation - drives this toward homochirality. One source, a small bias, one end.

[the ground] Enantiomeric excess and the inequality product_ee > seed_ee are exact arithmetic, sealed. THAT a near-symmetric start amplifies to one hand in the lab is the 2026 Nobel discovery of Kagan and Soai - cited, inferred from their experiments, never sealed here.
marks.source: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026; Kagan (1986); Soai (1995)

marks.claim: [declined] How life came to use a single handedness (L-amino acids, D-sugars) is the open origin question this illuminates but does not close; the engine seals the ee arithmetic and the amplification inequality, not the account of life's beginning.
